mcat_description.short: MS Porta Cabin is a prefabricated, portable structure fabricated from mild steel sections and GI/MS sheet cladding, sold as a complete unit or in knock-down form for on-site assembly. It serves as a temporary or semi-permanent space solution for offices, accommodation, storage, and security at construction and industrial sites.
mcat_description.long: An MS Porta Cabin is a factory-built modular enclosure constructed on a mild steel base frame (typically 100mm×50mm C-channel or I-beam) with MS/GI corrugated sheet exterior cladding, glass wool insulation (25–50mm walls, 50–80mm roof), interior MDF or pre-laminated board panelling, and PVC vinyl or cement board flooring. Cabins are supplied in standard sizes (10×10 ft, 10×15 ft, 10×20 ft being most common) or fully customised to buyer dimensions, and can be delivered as a plain shell or factory-fitted with electrical wiring, plumbing, windows, and furniture. The primary market is construction project sites, industrial plants, and infrastructure projects requiring rapid, relocatable workspace or accommodation without permanent civil construction. Buyers include construction contractors, infrastructure developers, industrial facility managers, and government project offices procuring for site offices, labour bunkhouses, security guard rooms, and storage units.

market_context: MS Porta Cabin is the dominant material-specific sub-category within the broader portable cabin market in India, distinguished from FRP, PUF panel, and Aerocon panel variants by its mild steel structural frame and GI/MS sheet cladding. The Indian market is highly fragmented with hundreds of small-to-mid-size fabricators concentrated in Maharashtra (Thane, Mumbai, Pune, Raigad), Gujarat (Ahmedabad), Delhi-NCR, Karnataka (Bengaluru, Ballari), and Telangana (Hyderabad). Standard commercial sizes are 10×10 ft, 10×15 ft, and 10×20 ft, with custom dimensions widely available; structural frames use 100mm×50mm C-channel or I-beam base frames with 50mm×50mm MS square pipe uprights. Insulation is typically 25–50mm glass wool for walls and 50–80mm for roofs, with GI corrugated sheet exterior and MDF/pre-laminated board interior panelling. No single BIS/IS standard governs the complete MS Porta Cabin assembly; component materials reference IS grades (IS 2062 for structural steel, IS 277 for GI sheets). Buyers transact primarily per piece for standard sizes and per sq ft for large custom configurations. The product serves a dual market: B2B construction/industrial procurement (dominant) and a growing B2C/residential segment (rooftop rooms, terrace cabins, portable houses) evidenced by keyword data. Container-style MS cabins (resembling ISO shipping containers) are a premium sub-type increasingly used for container cafes, portable homes, and modular offices.
